entities.label: Institution
entities.summary:
Edge, founded in 1993, is a British multi-format video game magazine and website that has played a crucial role in the evolution of video game journalism and culture. It emerged during a transformative period for the video game industry, characterized by rapid technological advancement and rising consumer interest, particularly in the United Kingdom and globally. Key figures involved in its foundation include the founding editors, who sought to elevate video game critique to a more serious and analytical level, influencing not only the UK market but also establishing a benchmark for similar publications worldwide.

The magazine distinguished itself through its in-depth reviews, features on game development, and coverage of industry trends. It was one of the first to adopt a more sophisticated editorial approach, providing insights into game design and the cultural implications of gaming. Throughout the 1990s and 2000s, Edge garnered a reputation for its high-quality journalism, often giving voice to emerging game developers and highlighting significant changes in the gaming landscape, such as the transition from 2D to 3D graphics and the rise of online gaming.

The legacy of Edge is evident in how it shaped both public perception and industry standards for video game journalism. Numerous journalists and critics who began their careers at Edge have gone on to influence media across various platforms, including television and online streaming. By fostering a culture of critical analysis, Edge contributed to the legitimization of video games as a serious art form, paving the way for academic inquiries into game studies and interactive media.
